`deliverer_router` is the module that `http_router_backend/v1` generates, and it holds only what that
backend emits. It imports the route handlers of `deliverer_api`, so `deliverer_api` cannot import it
back. The router declares its extractor of the `Authorization` field and names `check_token` as the
resolver of its one principal, but no route it serves calls them: the health route needs no token, and
every route that does is a handler of `deliverer_api`, which reads the field and calls `check_token`
itself, before the project id or the body.

Every other route passes the request to its handler in `module:deliverer_api`, which checks the
token, the project id and the form of its body when it has one, calls one operation of `module:photo_delivery` and
turns its refusal into an answer.
judgement.divergence: One implementation gives the handlers raw Authorization-field multiplicity and unparsed identifiers and bodies, while another gives them framework-normalized values; the calling flow notices unauthorized or invalid requests being refused versus reaching photo_delivery, and the router generator sees incompatible handler interfaces.
judgement.why: The four imported public operations have no State 5 contracts fixing their semantic inputs, outputs, errors, effects, callers or state impacts.

topics.topic: Handling failures while reading source-file entry metadata
questions: Does this include failure of the entry metadata reading, which A1 says refuses the whole scan unless the file disappeared, or only failure after a regular file has been identified and opened?

quotes:
When the listing reaches an entry, one metadata reading of that
entry in its opened folder, without following a link, decides that it is a regular file and gives its
listed size and modification time; an entry that reading does not show as a regular file is not
reported, and a reading that fails other than for a file that disappeared refuses the scan with
the FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode.

A file is then opened in that same opened folder: an opening that fails, or a failed metadata reading of the opened file,
is order 5, and an opened object that is not a regular file is order 3; either ends the work on that file
before any byte is read.
judgement.why: A1 distinguishes failed entry metadata, which refuses the scan unless the file disappeared, from failure after the file is opened, which is the per-file order-5 rejection.

topics.topic: Preserving directory identity between containment checking and traversal
questions: How is the identity of the checked directory preserved between containment checking and later traversal when only a path is returned?

quotes:
The photo folder is then reached by that
   resolved path, opened one folder at a time from the root of the file system without following a link
   at any of them (A1), so the folder that is read is the folder whose containment was checked; a folder
   on that path replaced after the check by a link or by anything that is not a folder cannot be opened,
   and the scan is refused with the FOLDER_UNAVAILABLE member of = models.RefusalCode or the delivery fails under condition 1 of A3 rule 5.

A folder is listed, its entries
are read and its files are opened only through the folder that was opened, so an entry replaced by a link
after a check is never followed.
judgement.why: The rules require reopening the resolved path component by component without following links and require refusal rather than traversal when a checked component has been replaced.
